subject: [PATCH] io_uring/sqpoll: do the return-to-userspace work in the SQPOLL thread

reviews.author: Jens Axboe
reviews.summary: Identified the root cause of the issue and suggested a straightforward fix to add a call to resume_user_mode_work() when TIF_NOTIFY_RESUME is set.
reviews.raw_body:
On Sat, 31 Oct 2026 19:21:46 -0700, Shakeel Butt wrote:
> The SQPOLL thread never returns to userspace. io_sq_tw() runs its
> task_work, but the rest of resume_user_mode_work(), like memory.high
> reclaim and block cgroup throttling, only runs when the thread exits.
> So memory.high reclaim only happens inside a charge, with sqd->lock and
> ctx->uring_lock held, and not at all if the charges can't block.
> 
> This used to work. The loop called io_run_task_work(), which does this
> work since commit b5d3ae202fbf ("io_uring: handle TIF_NOTIFY_RESUME
> when checking for task_work"). Commit af5d68f8892f ("io_uring/sqpoll:
> manage task_work privately") replaced that call with io_sq_tw().
> 
> [...]

Applied, thanks!

[1/1] io_uring/sqpoll: do the return-to-userspace work in the SQPOLL thread
      commit: f013b695506491c5202a412a6568313549c81f50

Best regards,
-- 
Jens Axboe

2026-11-03.patch_summary: The patch addresses a long-standing issue where the SQPOLL thread fails to return to userspace, causing memory.high reclaim and block cgroup throttling to occur inside a charge instead of at the top of the loop. This is due to a change in commit af5d68f8892f that replaced the call to io_run_task_work() with io_sq_tw(). The patch adds a call to resume_user_mode_work() when TIF_NOTIFY_RESUME is set, ensuring that these tasks run outside of the charge.
